issues.title: Missing ConfigureAwait(false) on Task.Yield
issues.description: The rule requires all await expressions in library code (non-test, non-sample projects) to use .ConfigureAwait(false) to avoid capturing the synchronization context, but the await Task.Yield() expression at line 291 omits it.
issues.rule_name: Async Methods Must Use ConfigureAwait(false) in Library Code

issues.title: Logout validation incorrectly rejects valid logout requests when HistoryEntryState is null
issues.description: The sign-out validation logic was modified to remove the null check for Navigation.HistoryEntryState before calling ValidateSignOutRequestState(). This causes ValidateSignOutRequestState() to return false when HistoryEntryState is null (since GetCachedNavigationState() returns null), which incorrectly redirects users to the logout failure page even for legitimate logout operations. The original code correctly allowed logout when HistoryEntryState is null by using the condition 'HistoryEntryState != null && !ValidateSignOutRequestState()', which only validated if state existed. This breaks backward compatibility with logout flows that don't use history state.

issues.title: Missing null check for InteractiveRequestUrl causes potential null reference in navigation
issues.description: The Redirect() method condition was changed from checking both InteractionOptions and InteractiveRequestUrl to only checking InteractionOptions. This creates a bug where if InteractionOptions is not null but InteractiveRequestUrl is null, the code will call NavigateToLogin with a null URL parameter at line 40. The NavigateToLogin method expects a non-null URL, so this will cause a null reference exception or navigation failure. The original PR properly validated both properties before choosing the navigation method.

pr.title: Code Review Bench PR #62755 - [Blazor] Remove obsolete APIs from Components

structured_output.summary:
This PR removes a batch of [Obsolete] Blazor APIs across Components, Forms, Web, WebAssembly, and WebAssembly.Authentication: Router.PreferExactMatches, the AddDataAnnotationsValidation and parameterless EnableDataAnnotationsValidation extensions, RemoteBrowserFileStreamOptions, the WebEventCallbackFactoryEventArgsExtensions class, WebRenderer.RendererId init, JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged, SignOutSessionStateManager, the obsolete RemoteAuthenticationService and AccessTokenResult constructors, and AccessTokenResult.RedirectUrl. The bulk of the mechanical work is sound. I grepped the head tree and found no remaining references to the removed public APIs, and PublicAPI.Shipped.txt files are untouched as required.

Beyond the deletions, the PR changes runtime behavior in three places the description does not fully explain. ProcessLogOut now fails whenever the history state is not a valid sign-out request, including when it is null, which contradicts the description's claim. It also adds an unexplained Task.Yield with a misleading comment. AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect drops its null guard on InteractiveRequestUrl. The PR also removes the test covering the logout failure path without adding a replacement. Separately, the PublicAPI.Unshipped entry for a ResourceAsset constructor has no matching source change in the diff, and an InternalCalls.InvokeJS binding is removed without being mentioned in the description.
structured_output.verdictRationale: Nothing here is a clear security or data-loss issue, but several items should be resolved or explained before merge: the unexplained Task.Yield with a misleading comment, the ResourceAsset PublicAPI entry that documents a removal the diff never makes, the dropped null guard in Redirect(), and the logout behavior change that the description states the other way round. The InvokeJS binding removal also needs confirmation that the native runtime no longer references it.

architecture.overview:
Blazor's WebAssembly authentication flow routes sign-out through RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore. NavigationManagerExtensions.NavigateToLogout puts an InteractiveRequestOptions state into the history entry, and ProcessLogOut validates that state before calling AuthenticationService.SignOutAsync. Token acquisition works similarly: RemoteAuthenticationService returns an AccessTokenResult, and AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect uses it to navigate to the login endpoint. Before this PR, both flows had backward-compatibility branches: a SignOutSessionStateManager session-storage check when history state was null, a RedirectUrl fallback, and an obsolete AccessTokenResult constructor.

The PR deletes those compatibility paths along with the other [Obsolete] surfaces listed in the description. The sign-out flow now depends solely on the history state, and token redirects depend solely on InteractiveRequestUrl and InteractionOptions. The Redirect() null guard was removed, and Task.Yield was added to ProcessLogOut.
steps: Entry point: NavigationManagerExtensions.NavigateToLogout writes InteractiveRequestOptions into the history entry state before navigating to the logout endpoint.

RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.ProcessLogOut now checks only ValidateSignOutRequestState(), and on failure navigates to LogOutFailedPath. The SignOutManager fallback that used to handle null state is gone. A new Task.Yield sits before AuthenticationProvider.GetAuthenticationStateAsync.
On success, AuthenticationService.SignOutAsync runs as before. The Mono/JSInterop layer loses the InternalCalls.InvokeJS binding, which is not referenced by any managed code in the tree.

Token path: AccessTokenResult now has only the four-argument constructor and InteractiveRequestUrl. AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect() branches on InteractionOptions alone, and the else branch navigates to InteractiveRequestUrl.
Surface area: PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt records *REMOVED* entries for each deleted symbol. The Components entry for the ResourceAsset constructor has no corresponding source change in this diff.

findings.title: Unexplained Task.Yield with a misleading comment in ProcessLogOut
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` (around lines 290-291) contains an unexplained `await Task.Yield();` with the comment "Ensure we're authenticated before proceeding with sign-out", which does not describe what yielding does. Either remove the yield and its comment if it isn't needed, or, if a dispatcher-ordering reason exists, replace the comment with the actual reason and add a test in `RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs` that demonstrates the behavior it guards against. Do not change the `isauthenticated` check.

findings.title: Logout failure path loses its test and the description misstates behavior
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/RemoteAuthenticatorViewCore.cs`, `ProcessLogOut` (around lines 281-287) now rejects any logout where `ValidateSignOutRequestState()` is false, including when `Navigation.HistoryEntryState` is null. The PR description claims the opposite. Confirm this is the intended behavior for removing `SignOutSessionStateManager`. Then add a test in `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/test/RemoteAuthenticatorCoreTests.cs` that calls the LogOut action with no history state and asserts navigation to `authentication/logout-failed` with the message "The logout was not initiated from within the page." Match the style of the deleted test. Also correct the PR description's sentence about null state.

findings.title: Null guard dropped from AccessTokenNotAvailableException.Redirect
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly.Authentication/src/Services/AccessTokenNotAvailableException.cs`, `Redirect()` (around lines 38-45) now checks only `_tokenResult.InteractionOptions != null` before calling `_navigation.NavigateToLogin(_tokenResult.InteractiveRequestUrl, ...)`. `InteractiveRequestUrl` is `string?`, so this is a nullable warning and can pass null through. Restore the null check on `InteractiveRequestUrl` in the first branch so the `NavigateToLogin` branch is taken only when both values are present, and keep the else branch using `InteractiveRequestUrl`. Make sure the else path handles a null URL deliberately, for example by throwing an InvalidOperationException, instead of relying on the `!` suppression.

findings.title: PublicAPI entry documents a ResourceAsset constructor removal that the source does not make
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/Components/src/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, line 2 records `*REMOVED*` for a `ResourceAsset(string! url, IReadOnlyList<ResourceAssetProperty!>? properties)` constructor. `src/Components/Components/src/ResourceAsset.cs` has no such overload at either base or head, and the shipped constructor has a default value. Check whether an obsolete overload was meant to be removed here. If not, delete the stale `*REMOVED*` line. If it was, remove the overload from `ResourceAsset.cs` and keep the entry. Also update the PR description so it matches what the diff actually does.

findings.title: InternalCalls.InvokeJS removed without mention in the description
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/JSInterop/src/InternalCalls.cs`, the `[MethodImpl(InternalCall)] InvokeJS<T0,T1,T2,TRes>` binding was removed. Its comment says it must match an entry in Mono's `driver.c` and exists only for backwards compatibility. Confirm with the WebAssembly runtime owners that the native driver no longer references this entry in any supported runtime version. Then either keep the removal and add a note to the PR description, or restore the binding. Do not change the JSImport-based `InvokeJSJson` path.

findings.title: Unusual ~ prefix in a *REMOVED* PublicAPI entry
findings.body:
The `NotifyLocationChanged(string uri, bool isInterceptedLink)` entry in `WebAssembly/src/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt` is written as `*REMOVED*~static ...`. This is the only `*REMOVED*~` in the repo. The other removed entry for the same method uses the plain `*REMOVED*static ...(string! uri, ...)` form. The `~` prefix is what the API analyzer emits in some nullability cases, so this may be generated output, but it is worth confirming that it matches what the analyzer produces and that the build passes with it.

::diff{file="src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly/src/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt" lines="1-3"}
findings.fixPrompt: In `src/Components/WebAssembly/WebAssembly/src/PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, line 2 uses a `*REMOVED*~static` prefix for `JSInteropMethods.NotifyLocationChanged`. No other PublicAPI file in the repo uses `~` this way. Regenerate the file with the PublicApiAnalyzer code fix or build and compare the output. If the analyzer produces the `~` form, leave it. If not, use the form that matches the rest of the repo.

findings.title: Most removals are clean and leave no stale references
findings.body: I grepped the head tree for every removed public symbol. The only remaining `PreferExactMatches` is a parameter on a test-only `CustomRouter`, which defines its own property and is unaffected. The `EnableDataAnnotationsValidation(editContext, serviceProvider)` overload used by `DataAnnotationsValidator` and a test `.razor` file still exists. `RendererId` is a getter-only property backed by `_rendererId`, so removing the `init` accessor needs no subclass changes. Shipped PublicAPI files were left alone, as the PR states.
